commits.summary: Example 285 is decided: its four proof tasks have their receipts, each as expected, and its blockers are closed
commits.body:
Example 285 (CVE-2023-34055, Spring Boot's WebMvcTags.method(HttpServletRequest)) had every proof task refused before any proof (VF-027). With jvmcontract extended in the three commits before the pipeline's (lvvpsuxl, lustnxwm, oyvynrux), the unchanged claims were rerun on the released JARs by its own checker under strict gaps, and the pipeline collected the receipts in xkplwmyz: vulnerable-security refuted on 2.7.17 (witness request.getMethod() = "", the label ImmutableTag{key="method", value=""}, run on a JVM), fixed-security established on 2.7.18, mutant-security refuted on the mutant (the same witness), and preservation established between 2.7.17 and 2.7.18, each release on its own pinned closure. Each is as expected and not vacuous; the verifier's runs took 0.2 to 0.4 s.

This commit brings the example's records in line with the receipts. target.json lists no blocker (the four observed ones and the two predictions are removed) and its handoff says what is decided and what the claims leave open; each records/refusals/TASK.json keeps the refusal as it was observed and gains `closed`, naming the job and the receipt that decided the claim; example.json's summary, verdict label and notes say what was proved and about which domain (an implementation of HttpServletRequest that answers getMethod() with one non-null String of at most 8 code units, or a null request); the page's two blocker sections are replaced by 'The proofs' and 'Closed gaps'. The router and examples/gap-inventory.md are regenerated: 21 blocked obligations in five observed gaps, where there were 25; two-dependency-closures now blocks three tasks (286, 287 and 306's preservation, whose route no longer refuses them, so their rerun checks will fail as not predicted and their ordinary attempts will say what else each needs) and interface-parameter four (305's). VF-027 has a dated update saying so.

The tests that pinned the blocked state follow: test_gap_inventory.py's ranking, totals, dated predictions (285's two are gone) and closure tasks; test_workflow_refusal.py's table of blocked tasks (21), its rerun example (286's preservation, since 285's is decided), and a new test that a closed gap blocks nothing, predicts nothing, leaves the task executable and names a receipt that decided the unchanged claim as expected; test_acceptance.py accepts an earlier unresolved receipt of a task whose packet is closed. Verified by the Python half of the default run (32 of 33 suites, the one failure being the cost inventory's lint on the renamed tests, fixed with test_costs.py estimate and rerun with the three changed suites); nothing under lib/src or lib/tests changed since the last Rust run.

A correction to the previous commit's message (oyvynrux): it said the second heap proof-tier job, 20261115-181435-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, was withdrawn before it started. The runner had started it at 18:25 UTC from the commit that queued it, before the commit that removed its job file landed; it was stopped, and its leftover result set aside (VF-029). The first one (20261115-173209-object-comparisons-under-jbmc-and-auto-c, at lvvpsuxl) failed on the four claims of VF-018, where JBMC does not finish in 600 s, as it did before these changes; its other five tests passed.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: claims javac compiles, String and String[] inputs, String, stream and regex models, induction and lemmas, for example 286's decision claim (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 286 (CVE-2022-22968, Spring Framework 5.3.18 to 5.3.19) states its decision claim in Java over the adapter entry allowed(String[] allowedPatterns, String[] disallowedPatterns, String field): a field some disallowed pattern matches ignoring ASCII case is denied, the match written with streams, lambdas and java.util.regex. Until now jvmcontract refused it at the String[] parameters, at the expressions, and at every String, StringBuilder, stream and regex call on the way. With this change the unchanged claim is proved on 5.3.19 and refuted on 5.3.18 and on the constructed mutant at small bounds inline (3 code units and 3 elements: 8 s, 7 s and 6 s in an unoptimized build), each witness run in the harness on a JVM; the frozen bound of 8 is queued.

What a property check gained. A String parameter is a String of its own of at most --max-array-length code units, and a String[] an array of such Strings or nulls. An assumption or assertion the tool's own expression compiler does not take is compiled by javac into a class beside the harness and run as bytecode, as the target is; a witness of such a claim is run in the harness on a JVM, so a refutation rests on Java's own libraries and not on a model. prove --decreases EXPR proves a method that calls itself by induction on a measure: a recursive call on arguments within the assumption and the bound whose measure is smaller is taken to satisfy the property, and any other recursive call ends the check with no verdict. prove --lemmas FILE proves each lemma first and then lets its statement stand in for the calls of its method where the arguments are within the bound it was proved at, the method running as written elsewhere; a method that writes a field or compares its arguments by identity is refused as a lemma's subject.

What the own checker gained. String.substring, indexOf, endsWith, toLowerCase on ASCII (under the stated assumption that the default locale is not Turkish, Azeri or Lithuanian), split at one character and chars; StringBuilder's constructors, length, indexOf, substring, delete and toString; lambdas, method references and four stream model classes run as the loops they stand for; Pattern.quote, String.join, Pattern.compile, matcher and matches as far as a claim states a glob with them, a pattern held as its pieces so that a case-insensitive match and an exact match of lower-cased Strings are one formula; class literals, Class.forName and the class path's loader under a stated assumption, for spring-jcl's logging probes. Each new String method has an evidence record in values::OPERATIONS (String model 3) whose 85 boundary cases give one outcome on the JVM, in the interpreter and in the checker; the interpreter's substring and toLowerCase now return the JDK's objects (the String itself, the literal empty String). What a model takes for granted about the JVM is listed among a statement's assumptions.

Paths. Once more than 1024 paths have been explored (Options::merge_heaps_after), paths whose heaps are not of one shape are merged into the union of their heaps, each first rid of dead locals and unreachable objects; a loop's exit is then a join, and waiting paths are resumed in the order of the loops they are in. Below that count the engine merges as before. The count is a measured compromise: merging heaps from the first path took the values sweep's list totals from 0.07 s to over a minute at 6 lines, since the two sums are then no longer one formula by gate hashing, and waiting for 1024 paths costs example 286's decision 1.7 times its time at 5 code units against 512. An array of computed size is taken within one more than the bound (a table over a bounded String's positions).

Two leaks found by the default run and closed. The new StringBuilder, Class and ArrayList models had been added to gaps::exact_jdk_call, which JBMC's gap listing and the contract reader also ask: JBMC's stubs for those calls would have counted as exact, and a contract for StringBuilder.<init>() was refused. They are now gaps::modelled_jdk_call, the own checker's alone, and a contract given for a modelled call is applied in place of the model, so the three contract tests of lib/tests/integration.rs pass unchanged. And a call the checker has no model of on a builder it holds the content of (append, reverse) now drops that content: a later modelled call on the builder is refused by name instead of answering from stale content.

examples/286-.../proofs/prove.py TASK runs vulnerable-security, fixed-security or mutant-security from target.json and the frozen claim file, on the revision's pinned JARs (each checked against its SHA-256) with the adapter compiled against them, and builds the mutant as sources.lock.json says. proofs/simple-match.contract is the lemma: PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch on ASCII Strings is the claim's own regular expression, by induction on the pattern's length. These are proofs beside the example route, which runs the verifier on the original artifact alone and still stops at DataBinder's receiver (VF-027); the example's records are not changed in this commit and follow with the results.

commits.summary: Example 286's decision claim is decided beside the route: established on 5.3.19, refuted on 5.3.18 and on the mutant, at the frozen bound
commits.body:
The three decision jobs queued with zrzuurtk have finished, each as expected, on the unchanged claim claims/disallowed-field-denied-ignoring-case.json through the adapter entry its first assumption names, with maxArrayLength 8, unwind 16, the own checker and strict gaps. fixed-security (job 20261115-234439-example-286-fixed-security-through-the-a): established on Spring Framework 5.3.19 in 920 s after the simpleMatch lemma's own proof in 92 s (4,889 paths, 2.6 million variables, 8.7 million clauses, 1.41 GiB), not vacuous; its trial at 6 took 189 s. vulnerable-security (20261115-234439-example-286-vulnerable-security-through): refuted on 5.3.18 in 409 s at allowed(allowedPatterns={"**", null, null, null, null, "", "", ""}, disallowedPatterns={"_Y[]*US"}, field="_Y[]  uS"), which returns true. mutant-security (20261115-234440-example-286-mutant-security-through-the): refuted on the constructed mutant in 398 s at allowed(allowedPatterns=null, disallowedPatterns={null, null, null, null, null, null, "*Y"}, field=" yzzy"). Both witnesses were run in the harness on a JVM (JDK 25.0.5), so the refutations rest on the releases' bytecode and Java's own java.util.regex, not on a model. The results themselves are collected by the verification loop; this commit cites them by job.

The example's records say what was decided and what was not. README.md has a section with the verdicts, the witnesses, how to rerun (python3 proofs/prove.py TASK), what the proof is (the lemma by induction, one meaning for a regular expression) and what the verdicts rest on (the lemma, the checker's models of the JDK calls on the way, and two stated assumptions about the locale and the class loader). example.json has four dated notes and a verdict label. In target.json the three predicted blockers the proofs reached each keep their text and gain a dated note saying they were reached and closed outside the route, the fourth (the bean wrapper's reflection) a note that it is still not reached, and handoff.next says what is next. VF-027 has an update line.

Not decided, and said so: these are proofs beside the route, not route receipts. The route runs the verifier on the original artifact alone, has no adapter entry and passes no lemma, so all six proof tasks stay blocked there, their packets and rerun checks unchanged. preservation, tried through the adapter entry, stops at the String[] parameter in the regression check; the protected-state tasks stop at java.util.ArrayList.<init>(int) in MutablePropertyValues.<init>, before the bean wrapper's reflection. The proof-tier job queued with zrzuurtk (20261115-234440-the-proof-tier-after-example-286-s-engin) is still running.

commits.summary: CLAUDE.md: a probe of a prover or model checker may run inline up to 5 minutes and 4 GB, under a cap
commits.body: At the user's request: the 1 GB line between inline runs and verification jobs had agents tuning a checker's memory to fit a quick probe before knowing whether the real proof works (prove-examples, example 287), and real-world claims often need more than 1 GB just to show where a checker stops. A single probe on one claim may now run inline, one at a time, for up to 5 minutes and 4 GB, inside systemd-run --scope with MemoryMax=4G and a timeout, so it cannot take more. A run that needs more is still a job, and the default test run and the tool tier keep their 1 GB. CLAUDE.md and verification/README.md say the same.

Conformance passed.

commits.summary: jvmcontract: loops beyond the bound covered by invariants, constant regexes, text as bytes and digits, for example 287's bcrypt claims (verification pending)
commits.body:
Example 287 (CVE-2025-22228: BCrypt.hashpw ignores bytes past 72) asks whether checkpw rejects a password of more than 72 bytes for every valid stored hash. The tool's own checker stopped at the claim's regular expression, at the text-to-bytes calls and at bcrypt's loops, which go round 18, 512, 2^cost and 64 times against --unwind 16. It now runs the claims as they are written. A loop that goes round more often than the bound is covered by an invariant the checker finds and proves by induction (lib/src/bmc/loops.rs: what one iteration writes is set to any value, candidate facts about each written number are dropped until the rest is kept by an iteration, and the loop is shown to end by a counter or said not to be); a verdict names the loops so covered, a violation past one is believed only when its witness, the least violating input, reproduces on a JVM, and otherwise the answer is no verdict with the loop named. Also new: String.matches and Pattern.compile of a constant regular expression with classes, groups, alternatives and counts (lib/src/bmc/regex.rs); String.getBytes(UTF_8), MessageDigest.isEqual, Arrays.copyOf, Integer.parseInt and StringBuilder's charAt and appends (lib/src/bmc/bytes.rs, strings.rs); Object.getClass of an object the run made, String.toString, an initializer that keeps method references, and a throws clause whose condition javac compiles. The solver side defers clauses until a call depends on them, checks lazy divisions only in the cone a question reads, and shares a path's models by pages. The search for the least witness takes at most half the time the run has left, so a violation found late is not lost to it.

The String model is model 4, the reference calls model 2: getBytes, matches and toString have evidence records sampled on the JVM and in the checker (lib/tests/values.rs), the gap scan counts Pattern.compile of a constant in the checker's syntax as reproduced, and the interpreter's String.toString returns the String itself. Tests that relied on a class regex, toString or a builder append being a gap now use forms that still are (a reluctant or possessive quantifier, trim, append(CharSequence), append(long)); the calibration fixture's RegexGate uses a possessive quantifier and its records were remade. New tests: lib/tests/loops.rs (four, on a small fixture with the same loop shapes), three in lib/tests/claims.rs (each model against a definition written out in Java and sampled on a JVM), three unit tests in bits.rs. Verified inline by the default run (python3 lib/tools/test_costs.py run: 34 of 34 passed).

Example 287 has proofs/prove.py, which runs the three security tasks beside the route through the adapter entry the claim names, and a dated note. One capped probe (5 minutes, 4 GiB) proved the byte-array guard claim on 6.3.8 at the route's bound in 250 s with six loops covered; the probe on 6.3.7 found its violating path and ran out of time minimising the witness, and the probe of the security claim through the adapter did not finish. None of these is a receipt. Jobs: 20261116-053832-example-287-fixed-guard-the-byte-array-g and 20261116-053832-example-287-vulnerable-guard-the-byte-ar (through the route), 20261116-053832-example-287-fixed-security-through-the-a, 20261116-053832-example-287-vulnerable-security-through and 20261116-053832-example-287-mutant-security-through-the (prove.py), and 20261116-053833-the-proof-tier-after-example-287-s-engin (the proof tier with --no-fail-fast and VF-018's three heap tests skipped, as VF-030 asks). Not attempted: the preservation task.

commits.summary: Receipts keep the loops an invariant covers beside the checker's numbers; example 287's guard tasks are queued again (verification pending)
commits.body:
The first runs of example 287's two guard tasks through the route (jobs 20261116-053832-example-287-fixed-guard-the-byte-array-g and 20261116-053832-example-287-vulnerable-guard-the-byte-ar) ran the verifier to its verdict, in 4m42s and 6m00s at 2.2 GiB, and were refused when the receipt was checked: build.py copied everything in the checker's statistics into search.native, which the result schema keeps for numbers, and the statistics now carry the list of loops covered by invariants (and, since example 286, what the models assume). search_record keeps the numbers in native and the two lists in search.loopsCoveredByInvariants and search.modelsAssume, both added to result.schema.json, with a unit test in examples/tools/test_build.py.

test_packets.py read example 287's review note as the last of its notes, which the note added with the previous commit displaced: it now finds the note by the review item it names. That failure was in the previous commit, whose default run was made before the note was added. Verified inline by the Python half of the default run (33 of 33 after the fix; the Rust sources are unchanged since the full run before the previous commit).

The three security jobs of the previous commit passed and are not collected yet: fixed-security established on 6.3.8 in 641 s, vulnerable-security and mutant-security refuted on a candidate of 25 code units and 73 bytes with a hash of cost 04, run on a JVM. Jobs queued here: 20261116-06*-example-287-fixed-guard-again-for-its-receipt and 20261116-06*-example-287-vulnerable-guard-again-for-its-recei (the ids are in verification/jobs).

commits.summary: Example 287's public claim is decided beside the route: established on 6.3.8, refuted on 6.3.7 and on the mutant, at the frozen bound
commits.body:
The three security jobs passed. fixed-security (20261116-053832-example-287-fixed-security-through-the-a): BCryptPasswordEncoder.matches on 6.3.8, through the adapter entry the claim names, throws IllegalArgumentException exactly when the candidate has more than 72 UTF-8 bytes and never returns true for one, for every candidate of up to 80 code units and every valid stored hash; 641 s, 641 paths, 3.0 GiB, six of bcrypt's loops covered by invariants the checker found and proved. vulnerable-security and mutant-security (20261116-053832-example-287-vulnerable-security-through, 20261116-053832-example-287-mutant-security-through-the): refuted in 819 s and 821 s on the least violating input, a candidate of 25 code units and 73 bytes with a hash of cost 04, where matches returns false instead of throwing; each witness was run on a JVM.

The example's README has a section on these proofs (what they are, what they rest on, how to run them, what is open), its entry a verdict label and a note, and target.json dated notes on the four predicted blockers, which were reached and closed, and on the observed ones. These are proofs beside the route, not route receipts: the route has no adapter entry. The two guard tasks, which do run through the route, reached verdicts and are queued again for their receipts (20261116-060128-example-287-fixed-guard-again-for-its-re, 20261116-060128-example-287-vulnerable-guard-again-for-i); their refusal packets stay as recorded until those are collected. Not attempted: preservation, and the guard claim on the mutant. Verified by the Python half of the default run (33 of 33).

commits.summary: Example 287: where the preservation claim stops beside the route
commits.body: Tried once through the adapter entry with each release's own class path (jvmcontract equivalence --before-classpath, which gets past the route's recorded gap of two dependency closures): a regression check refuses a nullable String parameter, and without the nullable parameters it refuses the allowed change as written, because a regression's scope is in the tool's own expression language, which has no getBytes. Recorded in the example's README and notes with the two refusals' words, and with what is predicted behind them and was not reached (pairing bcrypt's unchanged callees, since invariants that forget the S-boxes on each side cannot show two results equal). No code changed; the example's tests (test_packets, test_acceptance, test_gap_inventory, test_workflow_refusal, test_targets_contract, test_build, test_alignment) pass.

commits.summary: Record verification results for 8 jobs: example 287's three security claims as expected, the Rust proof tier passes with VF-018's three apart
commits.body: Jobs at 26a42d401510: 287's frozen public claim is established on 6.3.8 and refuted on 6.3.7 and on the char-count-guard mutant (as expected, 3 outputs each applied). The first two guard-lemma jobs failed with 'not-executed' (the receipt did not pass check_result); the submitter's reruns at c63eabcbd18b, 'again, for its receipt', passed as expected and applied the receipts. The proof-tier job (cargo --no-fail-fast, VF-018's three skipped) passed in 1h07m: conformance, heap and preparation ignored tests all ok. commits.summary: Example 287's guard lemma is decided by the route: established on 6.3.8, refuted on 6.3.7, and its two blockers are closed
commits.body:
The two guard tasks ran through the example route on the claim as frozen (claims/overlong-bytes-rejected.json on BCrypt.checkpw(byte[], String), arrays and Strings of up to 80, --unwind 16, own checker, strict gaps) and the pipeline collected their receipts in nkzzotot. fixed-guard (job 20261116-060128-example-287-fixed-guard-again-for-its-re, receipts/fixed-guard/20261116T070714Z-80d2813b): established in 244 s, not vacuous, six of bcrypt's loops covered by invariants. vulnerable-guard (job 20261116-060128-example-287-vulnerable-guard-again-for-i, receipts/vulnerable-guard/20261116T070828Z-a709a564): refuted in 318 s on 73 bytes with a hash of cost 04, where checkpw returns false and throws nothing, run on a JVM. The proof tier of the Rust tests after the engine changes passed as well (job 20261116-053833-the-proof-tier-after-example-287-s-engin, 1h07m, with --no-fail-fast and VF-018's three heap tests skipped, which is what VF-030 asked for).

This commit brings the example's records in line with the receipts, as example 285's were: records/refusals/fixed-guard.json and vulnerable-guard.json keep the refusal as observed and gain closed, naming the job and the receipt; target.json no longer lists those two blockers and its handoff says what is decided and what is next; the README has a section on the guard lemma, and its blocker table is split into the four tasks still blocked on the route and the two closed; example.json's verdict label and notes follow. The tests that pinned the blocked state follow too: test_workflow_refusal.py (19 blocked tasks, example 287's guard tasks among the closed ones, and the closed-gap test now asks that the sidecar lists no blocker for the closed task rather than none at all) and test_gap_inventory.py (the string-parameter gap blocks 3 obligations, 19 in all); examples/gap-inventory.md and the router are regenerated. Verified by the Python half of the default run (33 of 33).

Still open for example 287: the three security tasks have no route receipt (the route has no adapter entry; their claim is decided beside the route by proofs/prove.py), preservation, and the guard claim on the mutant.
